Review Text: I have taken a helicopter ride (except during the covid-19 shutdown) on nearly every visit to the islands since 1975. That is 102 visits to date. Review Text: We had the pleasure of flying with this company and with Blue Hawaiian. We flew around West Maui and Molokai with Blue Hawaiian. Although they were different trips, they were comparable in many ways. Both had excellent commentary from the pilots, both took safety very seriously, and both had an informative Hawaiian cultural aspect. Some of the things that set Maverick apart were the atmosphere in the lobby, the ability to land in a secluded, beautiful part of Hana rainforest, and the approachability of the pilot. The pilot came and greeted us personally and walked us to the aircraft at Maverick. We were pleased that none of the aircrafts around ours were on at that point, so it wasn't loud and our pilot talked to us about safety personally. At Blue Hawaiian, the other helicopters were on around ours, and we watched a video to learn about safety. Once we got into the helicopter, we each had our own headset to talk into, and we could hear everyone else in the helicopter. Overall, my fiance and I appreciated Maverick for its professional and personable employees. It was a lovely trip.

Review Text:

This trip takes you into the Rainforest...lands and you get to hike around seeing the taro, banana and pineapple plants. You get to see the coastal beaches and the sublime waterfalls. Review Text:
Although I originally scheduled flight got cancelled due to weather Maverick rescheduled us for later in the week which was fine, they cannot control the weather so there is nothing they can do about it.

The helicopters are brand new state of the art Airbus models with real air conditioning, excellent views from every seat and all the creature comforts needed.

Our pilot was awesome, he gave very good narration of the island, it's history etc the entire length of the flight. The landing in the Hana Rain Forest is worth the price of the tickets, they have staff there to take you on a guided tour of their property, explaining all about the rain forest, the vegetation, climate effects, animal (wild hogs) effects etc. We got to eat a banana right off the tree, see what's left of the taro crops that the hogs haven't destroyed, learn about the waterway going through the property and learn about the effects of humans on the islands native flora/fauna.

All in all, this was the highlight of our day, the pilot made sure to position the helicopter at every point so that everyone got a clear picture of what he was showing. Very safe, very comfortable and worth every penny to see something in a few minutes that would take 2 or more days to see by auto.
